tasks.gr10-job-market-lifelong-learning-t4: Topic: Job Market Trends, Qualifications and Lifelong Learning. Cover trends and demands in the job market (scarce skills, niches, reading the market from job adverts and news), the growth and decline of occupations and the competencies that last, SAQA (the South African Qualifications Authority), the National Qualifications Framework with its 10 levels (the National Senior Certificate at level 4, a bachelor's degree at level 7, a doctorate at level 10), recognition of prior learning, and lifelong learning (formal, non-formal and informal learning). Ask Grade 10 learners to identify a scarce skill or a niche, say what SAQA, the NQF or RPL is, work out the difference between two NQF levels, or classify a learning activity as formal, non-formal or informal.
tasks.gr10-religions-sport-bias-t4: Topic: Religions, Belief Systems and Fairness in Sport. Cover living in a multi-religious society (Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism, the Baha'i Faith and African religion, freedom of religion in the Bill of Rights, respect and understanding), ethical traditions and shared values such as caring for others, indigenous belief systems handed down by oral tradition, bias in sport (gender, race, stereotyping) and how to redress it, and unfair practices (drug-taking or doping, match-fixing, subjective umpiring, maladministration) with critical evaluation of a report. Keep every item respectful and neutral about religion: describe, never rank or ridicule a belief. Ask Grade 10 learners to match a religion to its holy book, choose a respectful response to a classmate of another faith, identify a kind of bias or an unfair practice, or choose a way to redress bias.
tasks.gr10-physical-education-t4: Topic: Physical Education: Traditional and Non-traditional Sport. Cover the difference between traditional and non-traditional sport, learning a sport in order (basic skills, rules, tactics), recording performance and improvement, fair play, rules and officials, and safety in sport (protective equipment, warm-up, technique, water, stopping when injured, and what to do after a knock to the head). Ask Grade 10 learners to classify a sport, put the steps of learning a sport in order, work out an improvement from a practice log, or choose the safe action after an injury.
